To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the time-scale of the hadronization process is crucial for the production of strange hadrons in heavy ion collisions.
the hadronic evolution of the system cannot drive it towards full chemical equilibirium, and that the time-scale of strangeness hadronization can be measured with balance functions.

1) the radial flow of strange baryons is a sensitive probe of the early stage of the reaction; 2) hadronic rescattering is not able to drive the system to full chemical equilibrium if hadronization occurs after the system has been out of chemical equilibrium; 3) balance functions are sensitive to the time-scales of hadronization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the early stages of relativistic nuclear collisions, and in particular the hadronization of the system.
the study of multi-strange hadron production in relativistic heavy-ion collisions, in the search for the onset of the QGP.
the study of the properties of the early phase of heavy ion collisions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the observed balance functions are not compatible with hadronization at a late stage of the reaction.
the time scale of the onset of strangeness production is a sensitive probe of the time-scale of the onset of hadronization.
the observed hadronization is consistent with a late-stage hadron formation scenario.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
strangeness production and the balance function are sensitive probes to the hadronization mechanism.
hadronization is a sensitive probe to study the dynamics of heavy-ion collisions.
strangeness production and the evolution of the system are intimately linked, and that multi-strange bariyons are sensitive probes to the hadronization dynamics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hadronization is a process that can be probed with precision, and that the resulting hadrons can be used to learn about the state of the system before hadronization.
the study of multi-strange hadrons in the future FAIR, NICA, and RHIC experiments can provide a unique probe to the hadronization process and the properties of the QGP.
the hadronization of the system is a crucial ingredient in determining the final state observables.
